subject: BrightBridge Health — Dedicated GPU sizing, isolation & SLA (recap)
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
Cc: Pete Morales <pete.morales@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightBridge call follow-up — dedicated capacity needs

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few open items so we stay aligned:

Pain points we mentioned:
- Latency spikes during morning surge (7–10am PT) — p95 jumps from ~200ms to >1.2s, impact on clinician workflows.
- High per-token inference costs when we run larger batches; want predictable unit economics.
- Regulatory: PHI in requests, need tenant isolation and audit logs for compliance.

Goals / constraints:
- Target steady-state throughput: ~300 req/s (avg seq length ~512 tokens).
- Burst to ~800 req/s for short windows (a few minutes).
- SLO: aiming for 99.9% availability, p95 < 800ms end-to-end for typical requests.
- Data residency: US-east preferred (we can discuss multi-region later).
- Procurement timeline: prefer to have procurement complete by end of Q2.

As discussed, can you provide a short, ballpark sizing and next steps for a reserved/dedicated deployment (isolation, SLA, rough cost)? Also we will send a security questionnaire to evaluate controls.

Thanks — Sara
—
Sara Chen
Director, AI Products
BrightBridge Health

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 5:05 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example> wrote:

> From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.example>
> To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@brightbridgehealth.com>
> Cc: Pete Morales <pete.morales@brightbridgehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
> Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: BrightBridge call follow-up — dedicated capacity needs
>
> Hi Sara / Pete — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed path forward so everyone has the same set of next steps.
>
> Summary of what we heard:
> - Primary outage surface is latency spikes at peak; you need predictable p95/p99 performance for clinician flows.
> - Data must be isolated (tenant-level segregation) and auditable (KMS + access logs).
> - Throughput profile: ~300 req/s steady, short bursts to ~800 req/s. Avg seq length ~512 tokens; some long-form generative jobs up to 2k tokens but infrequent.
> - Procurement timeline end of Q2 — procurement team will want a clear SOW + pricing sheet.
>
> Proposed dedicated configuration (ballpark):
> - Dedicated pool: 4x H100-equivalent nodes (ML-inference optimized) with autoscale headroom to add burst capacity up to ~2x baseline.
> - Model: FP16 + 8-bit quantized variant recommended for cost/latency tradeoff (we will test both).
> - Networking: VPC peering, customer-managed subnets, and optional on-prem connector for sensitive flows.
> - Security: KMS integration, customer audit logs, and SOC2 evidence (we will share the pack).
> - SLAs: target 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool; latency SLOs we can commit to for the baseline config (p50 ~40–60ms token-processing, p95 ~300–700ms depending on model/sequence length).
> - Ballpark committed cost: $40k–$55k / month depending on final node count, quantization strategy, and reserved term (1yr vs 3yr). We will provide a formal proposal with line items.
>
> Immediate next steps we suggest:
> 1) Confirm average tokens per request and % of long-form (>1024 tokens) requests (Sara).
> 2) Share a sampled traffic profile or anonymized request histogram so we can run a sizing sim (BrightBridge).
> 3) We will run a 1-week perf test on a sandbox dedicated pool (Ben to kick off).
> 4) Schedule a technical deep-dive to lock in node sizes and SLOs — propose Wed 7 Apr, 10am PT (option: Thu 8 Apr).
> 5) We will attach a draft SLA and throughput estimate for your legal/procurement review.
>
> Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla-draft-v1.pdf (attached), expected-throughput-estimates.xlsx (attached), MVP-deployment-diagram.png (attached).
>
> I’ll leave scheduling and the perf test action to Karthik / Ben but wanted to capture the high-level recap in one place.
>
> Thanks — Evelyn
>
> --
> Evelyn Hart
> Senior Director, Solutions 
> Redwood Inference
